title: OpenAI + @Temporalio : Building Durable, Production Ready Agents - Cornelia Davis, Temporal
talk_summary: Cornelia Davis explains Temporal as durable execution for agent workflows: activities are retried and event-sourced, workflows resume after crashes, and the OpenAI Agents SDK can run inside that model. The practical core is checkpointed LLM/tool calls, idempotent side effects, and queue-based workers rather than a single long-lived process.

takeaways.technique: Durable step journal for agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap each LLM call and tool call as a Temporal activity; event-source every request/return so a crashed worker resumes from the last completed step instead of restarting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We have kept track of every single LLM call and return and you will not be reburning those tokens.
takeaways.numbers: 1,350-second LLM turn cited as crash example

takeaways.technique: Idempotent activities with explicit retry policy
takeaways.what_they_do: Temporal retries activities automatically, but the speaker says developers must make side-effecting activities idempotent because retries can duplicate work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: activities themselves should be item potent

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a dynamic activity handler that looks up tool name in a tools module; swap tool sets without changing the agentic loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can swap in and out that tools module and the agentic code does not change at all.

takeaways.what_they_do: Build many small agents with independent loops and orchestrate them in code or via handoffs; handoff changes context/persona rather than starting a separate loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: build lots of small agents that have their own independent agentic loops and then orchestrate them together.

takeaways.what_they_do: Workflow can wait for human input for days/weeks; worker evicts it from memory/cache and reconstitutes state when signal arrives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: after a little bit more time, it'll come out of the cache and it'll be just as if you had just killed that process

takeaways.what_they_do: Workers pull workflows/activities from queues and are multi-threaded; scale by running more workers, not by one monolithic process.
takeaways.numbers: tens of milliseconds latency to Temporal server per activity call
